newsitem.title: KENYA: New Congo students protest Tutsi army.
newsitem.headline: New Congo students protest Tutsi army.

text.p: Students in the Democratic Republic of Congo's northeastern city of Kisangani demonstrated against the new government's army on Sunday and called for its withdrawal, a humanitarian source said on Monday.
Scores of students demonstrated in the city centre for up to four hours and said President Laurent Kabila was a hostage to ethnic Tutsis from Rwanda.

"There were protests on Sunday afternoon and also on Sunday evening. They were saying that Kabila is a hostage of the Tutsis and calling for an immediate retreat of foreign forces," the humanitarian source in Kisangani said.

The killing of a local political activist sparked Sunday's protest, the source said but gave no details. There was a heavy army presence in the city on Monday to prevent further protests, the source added.
Kabila declared himself president on May 17 after his forces entered the capital Kinshasa, ousting Mobutu Sese Seko at the end of a seven-month campaign starting on the country's eastern border.
The ruling Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (AFDL) banned demonstrations after it took power.
Ethnic Tutsi Rwandan troops played a key role in the rebellion but have proved unpopular in Kisangani, where students also demonstrated last month.

The U.N. Security Council called last week for an end to violence against Rwandan Hutu refugees in the east of the country following numerous reports of massacres. The government has denied the charges as intimidation.
